[RAZI-FULL:v13p79/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | rejects | Razi's second refutation notes that our horizon is another region's meridian: when the sun is up there at our midnight, it aligns with our eastern air, which still is not illuminated, disproving the claim that air receives and transmits its light.
[RAZI-FULL:v13p79/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Even if sunlight causes illumination, bodies share the same essence and extension; any distinguishing property must be a substrate, an inhering quality, or neither, and each option fails, so the sun's special power requires a voluntary creator.
